title: The bar is met, and the default deliberately stays 'ts'
description: With every divergence closed, the bar as originally written — equivalent: true — becomes satisfiable. Assert it directly, record that it is met, and say what a flip would now involve. This spec does not flip it.

successCriteria.description: The conformance harness reports equivalent: true on a real run of both engines, verified by running it.
The divergence-set pin becomes an equivalence assertion that still fails in BOTH directions — a new divergence fails it, and so does a silently-relaxed comparison.
docs/pge-graph.md's disposition is rewritten: which divergences closed and how, that the bar is met, and that the default stays 'ts' by choice rather than by blocker.
oracle-retention.test.ts still passes unmodified — pipeline.engine still defaults to 'ts', TsPipelineEngine is still selected and still the fallback.
Any field that did NOT converge is stated plainly with its reason, rather than the record implying total closure.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, and the golden gate passing at or above its replay floor.

nonGoals: Claiming closure for a field that did not converge.
stopConditions: equivalent: true is not reached — record exactly which field still diverges and why, and do not adjust the comparison to reach it. A spec that closed three of four honestly is worth more than one that claims four.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: This is the closing record; write it like one. The previous spec's closing section in docs/pge-graph.md is the model — it stated the outcome, named what was enforced by which test, and said what stayed unproven. The most valuable sentence here is the one that says what a flip would now actually require, now that the bar is no longer the blocker. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees. Verify on a CLEAN checkout, not just the working tree: this repo has twice been green locally and red in CI because uncommitted state was carrying the result.
evaluatorNotes: Verify equivalence by running the harness, not by reading the pin. Then mutation-test the new assertion in both directions. Finally read the prose against reality: every field it claims closed should be absent from a run you perform yourself. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees.
